subject: Model fit - playing with GUESS attributes

messages.author: 73db0f7e944f4290
messages.subject: Model fit - playing with GUESS attributes
parts:
Hi Chris,

I'm struggling to fit a good model to one individual animal's data. It seems that no matter what parameters I try, the fit looks bad and identical to each other. I've attached figures showing the fit with whatever parameters variogram.fit() gave me without moving the sliders (default) vs. when I played with the sliders (adjusted). Zoomed out is on the left, zoomed in on the right.


I see that this animal has an undulating semivariance pattern, especially at the shorter lags, so would changing GUESS$mean from stationary to non-stationary help?


Also, I was browsing the R package description & Variograms and Model Selection vignette and read about circular/elliptical covariances. I'm thinking changing GUESS$circle and/or GUESS$isotropic from FALSE to TRUE could help my model fit, but I don't understand what that would do. Can you please explain what circular/elliptical covariances are? In addition, what's GUESS$CPF?


Finally, please suggest anything else you think would help with my model fit. I've attached my data for this animal & code to this post for your reference.


Thank you,

-Emily

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Model fit - playing with GUESS attributes
parts:
Hi Emily,

The initial value of the guess only matters in as much as ctmm.fit() is able to find the maximum likelihood estimate with optim(). What you have is probably the right answer for that model.

A periodic mean from vignette("periodogram") will probably capture the daily oscillation, assuming that isn't a sampling artifact.
The hump at 1 month... you might try also adding in a lunar periodicity. I can't see if its periodic or stochastic from the variogram, though.
The isotropic argument is not going to help. isotropic=TRUE gives you VAR[x]=VAR[y] and COV[x,y]=0, while isotropic=FALSE relaxes this assumption. Its generally safe to leave that up to model selection.

For occurrence distributions, only the short-lag correspondence really matters, though, and it looks like you already have good fit a few lags out.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Model fit - playing with GUESS attributes
parts:
No, but lunar harmonics can make arbitrary periodic shapes.

Keeping things as simple as possible, the variogram you see is a sum of deterministic (mean/trend) and stochastic (autocorrelation function) movement components and telemetry error. That kind of tweaking of the model needs to be done at the level of the model components.

From what I can see of your variogram, it looks like there is a daily periodicity shifting around within monthly range (or monthly periodicity). Right now, only the latter is coded in the package, but the former will come within a year or so now that the Kalman filter code has been upgraded.

Best,
Chris
